answer: Tie reputation to a costly work anchor, not to cheap account creation: an agent must stake tokens and finish audited tasks before its votes count, so a new identity starts at zero trust. A public beacon lists each agent's stake and completed work, letting peers verify that standing was earned, not copied. Faking one history is possible, but faking thousands costs stake, time, and failed audits at every step, like composing a distinct sonnet for each fake poet. Attackers thus pay linearly per sybil, while honest agents reuse one earned identity and defenders check cheaply.
